query_text: Why do men have larger Adam's apples?

content.text:
Men typically have larger Adam’s apples because **testosterone during puberty makes the larynx grow**.

The “Adam’s apple” is the visible bump made by the **thyroid cartilage**, which surrounds the voice box/larynx. During puberty:

- **In males**, higher testosterone levels cause the larynx to enlarge significantly.
- The thyroid cartilage grows and tilts forward more, creating a more noticeable bump in the neck.
- A larger larynx also lengthens and thickens the vocal cords, which is why many boys’ voices deepen during puberty.

Women also have thyroid cartilage and can have visible Adam’s apples, but on average the larynx grows less during puberty, so the bump is usually smaller or less prominent.

So, in short: **men usually have larger Adam’s apples because male puberty enlarges the voice box more, mainly under the influence of testosterone.**
